title: Catastrophic Medical Hardship Under the Patient Hardship Discount Program: The Responsibility Cap
content:
At Catastrophic Medical Hardship, the Patient Hardship Discount Program discount on each charge is the part of that charge that takes the patient's responsibility for the period above 20% of annual household income.

## 1. The cap

The cap is annual household income multiplied by 20 and divided by 100, rounded to the cent. The 20% is the catastrophic share of Catastrophic Medical Hardship; every other level carries a share of 0 and has no cap.

## 2. The patient's responsibility for the period

The responsibility for the period is the total of the patient charges posted for the applicant and the covered dependents whose visit date falls from the determination's effective date through its expiry date, leaving out time-of-service deductible-estimate charges, less the amounts of the billing-error-correction and timely-filing write-off adjustments on those charges.

## 3. The discount on a charge

A charge is discounted by the part of it that lies above the cap once that charge is added to the responsibility for the period:

- if the responsibility, with the charge, stays at or below the cap, no part of the charge is above it;
- if the responsibility was below the cap and the charge carries it above, the discount is the amount by which the responsibility with the charge exceeds the cap;
- if the responsibility was already at or above the cap, the whole charge is above it and is discounted.

The discount is recorded with a percentage applied of 0, marking it as a catastrophic cap discount.

## 4. Worked schedule (hypothetical household)

Annual household income is $45000.00. The cap is $45000.00 multiplied by 20 and divided by 100: $9000.00.

| Charge | Responsibility before the charge | Charge amount | Responsibility with the charge | Part above $9000.00 | Discount | Patient owes on the charge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | $8400.00 | $300.00 | $8700.00 | $0.00 | $0.00 | $300.00 |
| B | $8700.00 | $500.00 | $9200.00 | $200.00 | $200.00 | $300.00 |
| C | $9200.00 | $150.00 | $9350.00 | $150.00 | $150.00 | $0.00 |

## 5. Effect of a correction (hypothetical)

Posted charges for the period total $9100.00, and a billing-error correction of $150.00 is recorded on one of them. The responsibility for the period is $9100.00 less $150.00, which is $8950.00 — below the $9000.00 cap. A deductible estimate posted in the period would not enter the total at all.
